cases.intro: The four faults reported first, and the two found while fixing them.
cases.title: Repeated tap raises the quantity
cases.pre: Counter paired; at least one product on the shelf.
cases.data: Any product with a price.
steps: Open the Sell screen.
The shelf list is shown on the left, the cart on the right.
Tap a product once.
One line appears in the cart, quantity 1.
Tap the SAME product again.
Still ONE line. The quantity box now reads 2.
Tap it a third time.
Quantity box reads 3, and the line total is 3 × the unit price.
cases.note: The first fault reported. The quantity was always right underneath; the box never repainted, so it read 1 beside ₹150 of a ₹50 item.

cases.intro: The four faults reported first, and the two found while fixing them.
cases.title: Enter adds the product that was typed
cases.pre: Sell screen open.
cases.data: The full name of a product that is NOT first in the list.
steps: Type the product name in full in the search box.
The list narrows; the typed product is highlighted.
Press Enter.
THAT product is added — not the first row of the list.
cases.note: Reported as "Enter adds the wrong product".

cases.intro: The four faults reported first, and the two found while fixing them.
cases.title: Search finds a name ending in a letter or a number-word
cases.pre: Sell screen open; a product named like "Nandhini milk 500 ml" exists.
cases.data: na m 500
steps: Type: na m 500
Nandhini milk 500 ml appears in the results.
Search a product whose name ends in a single letter (e.g. "Probe biscuit A").
It is found.
cases.note: "a", "an" and "oru" mean ONE to the numeral reader, so "Probe biscuit A" became "Probe biscuit 1" and matched nothing.

cases.intro: The four faults reported first, and the two found while fixing them.
cases.title: An offer on the shelf comes off the bill
cases.pre: A live offer exists that covers a category (e.g. buy 2 get 1 on Biscuits).
cases.data: Three units of a product in that category.
steps: Find a product showing an offer badge on its shelf row.
The badge names the offer.
Add three of it to the cart.
The cart line shows the discount.
Read the totals.
"Saved" shows the discount and TOTAL is reduced by it.
cases.note: The cart described a line without its category, so a category offer could never match — while the shelf badge did. The shelf promised what the bill refused.

cases.pre: Sell screen open.

cases.intro: The four faults reported first, and the two found while fixing them.
cases.title: A tiered price changes at the break
cases.pre: A product with a tiered pricing structure exists (e.g. 10+ at a lower rate).
cases.data: Buy 1, then buy the tier quantity.
steps: Add ONE of the tiered product.
The line uses the list price.
Raise the quantity to the tier break (e.g. 10).
The unit price CHANGES, and the line says "10+ price".
cases.note: The biggest fault found overnight: the counter skipped pricing entirely, so a tiered product billed at list price at the till while the storefront re-priced it. Same goods, two prices, depending which door the customer came through.

cases.pre: At least one line in the cart.
steps: Press − on a cart line.
The quantity falls by one.
Press + on the same line.
It rises by one.
Press Ctrl + Up arrow.
The LAST line rises by one AND the product list does not scroll or move.

cases.intro: The four faults reported first, and the two found while fixing them.
cases.title: The count and the tax split are shown
cases.pre: A GST-registered shop; three products in the cart totalling five items.
cases.data: 3 products / 5 items.
steps: Read the cart heading.
It reads "3 products · 5 items".
Read the totals block.
Taxable, then CGST and SGST on separate lines, then GST total.
Add CGST + SGST by hand and compare with GST total.
They are exactly equal (e.g. 3.34 + 3.33 = 6.67).
cases.note: CGST takes the rounded half and SGST the remainder — the tax engine's own rule.

cases.intro: How a bill is settled, and what gets recorded about it.

cases.pre: At least one line in the cart.
steps: Read the line under the Cash / UPI / Card buttons.
"This bill will be recorded as Cash."

The sentence changes to say Card.

cases.intro: How a bill is settled, and what gets recorded about it.
cases.title: UPI shows a QR for the amount due
cases.pre: Shop has a UPI payee declared in Settings; a bill open with an amount due.
steps: Tap UPI.
A QR code appears.
Read beside the QR.
It shows the amount, the payee id, and "The shop marks it paid here once the money arrives."
Scan it with any UPI app (do NOT pay).
The app shows the shop name and the correct amount.
cases.note: Nothing confirms the payment. The money moves bank to bank — a counter claiming to have SEEN it would be lying about what it cannot observe.

It reads "Paying you shows the name <your shop name>".
cases.note: That name appears in the customer's app before they press send. If it were a machine handle, that is how they decide not to.

The box holds 500.
Tap "+ part".
A part appears: "Cash ₹500.00 ×".
Tap UPI.
The line reads "Taking ₹500.00 in Cash · ₹X still due as UPI".

cases.intro: Migration b213 is run and verified. [TILL-07] covers the arithmetic automatically; these test the SCREENS, which no person has worked yet.
cases.title: Encashing does NOT change the total or the tax
cases.pre: REW-07 done; a customer with 100+ points; a bill of ₹500 open.
steps: Write down the TOTAL, the taxable value and the GST.
Three figures noted.
Press Encash.
A payment part appears: "Points ₹1.00".
Read the totals again.
TOTAL is UNCHANGED. Taxable is UNCHANGED. GST is UNCHANGED.
Read the amount still due.
It has fallen by ₹1.00.
cases.note: The one design decision worth arguing about. A discount would restate the taxable value, and those points came from an earlier sale already taxed — so the tax would come off twice and the SHOP answers for it at the return. Points pay for part of the bill instead, like cash and UPI already do.
